summary: Follow-up postmortem/check-in after Halo Health observed intermittent latency spikes and a short outage during high-concurrency nightly batch. Discussion covered immediate mitigations, deeper root-cause hypotheses (KV cache cold-starts + autoscaling thresholds + noisy background jobs), required telemetry and logs, compliance/security questions for private Dedicated deployment, and clear next steps for reproducing and validating fixes in staging.
topics: security/compliance for private deployment (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-09 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (Halo Head of Platform), Marco Diaz (Halo CTO), Emma Liu (Halo SRE), Samir Patel (Halo Security), Nina Gomez (Halo Product)

[00:00] Maya: Thanks everyone for joining, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes. Main goals — run through the postmortem draft, agree on mitigations, and set owners.
[00:12] Priya: Thanks Maya, yeah we had the spike last thursday night, about 2am our time, and it took down a few request queues for ~7 minutes. We're mainly worried about recurrence and our SLA calls.
[00:25] Jonah: Quick recap from our side — we saw concurrent tail latency rise when the nightly batch hit plus the q ingestion. There was evidence of KV cache cold starts, and a couple of workloads that weren't getting prefetched.
[00:38] Emma: Right, we saw spike in cache misses; also some pods scaled slowly, HPA didn't bring up enough replicas quick enough.
[00:48] Marco: To be clear, this is a customer-impacting outage, we need a remediation plan and a timeline.
[00:56] Maya: Absolutely. I sent a first-cut postmortem; today Jonah will walk through the technical evidence, and we'll agree mitigations.
[01:10] Jonah: Ok, quick screenless run-through — evidence shows token-level latency for generation queued up while KV cache warmed. I want to call out two things: the model variant fallback firing late, and the autoscaler thresholds were conservative — 70% CPU threshold which for elastic bursts is too slow.
[01:31] Priya: Are you sure about the fallback? We thought fallback should've been instant to a lower-capacity model.
[01:38] Jonah: The fallback triggers are per-route and per-model; with the specific route config it waited until the request queue length pass a threshold. Also there's a small mismatch in model compatibility so we delay a re-route to avoid hallucination regressions.
[01:52] Emma: We also noticed some big gc pauses on a backend job that overlapped with the spike. Might be a noisy neighbor effect.
[02:02] Samir: From a security perspective, we want to ensure logs we share are scrubbed — PHI can appear.
[02:09] Maya: Yes we'll scrub PII. We'll share an attached subset of logs.
[02:15] Priya: Can you clarify KV cache — are we talking Redwood's internal cache or our in-cluster redis?
[02:21] Jonah: It's the Redwood serving KV cache — the per-model key-value cache that stores prefixes/kv cache for attention, sometimes shorthand as KV-cache. In some transcriptions it's written as k v cache, sorry for the confusion.
[02:35] Nina: Is that configurable for TTL? We want to ensure pre-warm for nightly batch.
[02:40] Jonah: Yes TTL and prefetch settings exist; currently the default is lazy populate. We recommended an aggressive prewarm for heavy nightly runs.
[02:49] Marco: What's the path to test that? We have staging but not identical traffic shapes.
[02:55] Jonah: We can provide a staging runbook — two controlled runs: one with dedicated pool reserved for the run (to isolate noisy neighbor), and one on shared to measure improvement. We'll provide scripts and HPA examples.
[03:12] Priya: About dedicated vs hosted — we're evaluating Redwood Dedicated to avoid noisy neighbors. Any security caveats?
[03:20] Maya: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and isolation. For private deployments we can offer VPC peering, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit log exports. Samir, we know you asked about SOC2 artifacts — we can share our SOC2 report under NDA.
[03:34] Samir: Good. We also need to ensure KMS key management policies are compatible, and confirm if logs include token-level traces — we may need redaction.
[03:43] Jonah: On logging — we can provide token-level cost/latency breakdowns but we'll provide redacted versions. For forensic timelines we'll include request IDs and sampling.
[03:54] Emma: Operationally, my ask is that autoscaling be more aggressive, and introduce circuit-breaker for model fallbacks so we don't queue.
[04:03] Jonah: Agreed. Proposed mitigations: 1) Prewarm KV cache for nightly jobs; 2) Lower HPA threshold and faster scale-up (add target CPU 40-50% and reduce stabilization window); 3) Add a fallback model route with immediate re-route for 503s/latency SLO breach; 4) Isolate heavy background jobs to off-peak nodes.
[04:30] Priya: Do we expect cost impact from prewarm and dedicated pools?
[04:35] Maya: Yes there will be cost tradeoffs. Redwood Optimize can run cost/perf sims and provide a delta estimate.
[04:43] Marco: We need numbers — e.g., 10% cost increase vs 90% reduction in p95 latency.
[04:51] Jonah: We'll run two runs and provide token-per-second and cost-per-token estimates.
[04:57] Nina: On observability gaps — we couldn't trace the exact handoff between our queue and the model runtime. Anything you recommend?
[05:04] Jonah: Add request-id propagation end-to-end, increase trace sampling for the nightly window, and enable the Redwood per-route tracing hooks. Also we'll add more metric exports for KV hit/miss and per-model queue length.
[05:22] Emma: That should help.
[05:25] Maya: Ok let's talk timeline and owners. We'll send initial logs and the postmortem draft by EOD Friday (2026-12-11). Jonah will provide autoscale HPA configs and a runbook by Monday (2026-12-13). Halo runs staging validation by Wednesday (2026-12-15). We reconvene week of Dec 20.
[05:45] Priya: Sounds good. Two quick questions — one, will the dedicated pool fix this 100%? Two, can we get a change window to test?
[05:54] Jonah: Nothing is 100% but dedicated reduces noisy neighbor risk a lot; combined with prewarm and more aggressive autoscale, recurrence risk is low. We'll coordinate a maintenance window; Redwood Ops can assist.
[06:07] Samir: We'll need to review any new data flows for compliance — please include that in the security checklist.
[06:12] Maya: noted. Lena will own the doc.
[06:15] Lena: I'll set up the shared postmortem doc and invite owners.
[06:20] Marco: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the clarity.
[06:24] Maya: Quick recap in chat: Redwood to share timeline/logs and runbook; Jonah to share autoscale config; Halo to run staging tests. Follow-up call week of Dec 20.
[06:36] Priya: Thanks, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: recording auto-transcription had typical mis-hearing of KV-cache as "k v cache" and occasional speaker labeling errors (Emma and Priya sometimes swapped). Some technical terms (HPA, KMS, SOC2, SAML) were transcribed correctly intermittently.
